item.description: Serie A Preview: Venezia vs Inter – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Wednesday’s Serie A clash between Venezia and Inter has all the makings of a ‘David vs Goliath’ contest as the division’s last side encounters the high-flying reigning champions. The teams head into proceedings in starkly contrasting spirits after the weekend. Despite beating Napoli 1-0 in their last home outing, Venezia failed to build on their first win of the season as they found themselves on the receiving end of the same scoreline away to Genoa on Saturday. New manager Davide Nicola may have won on his touchline debut, but steering the Winged Lions away from the foot of the table could prove a Herculean task. Except for that shocking victory over Napoli, Venezia have lost all seven remaining league fixtures this season. However, they commence this midweek round only a point adrift of 17th-placed Udinese, meaning another unlikely win here could lift them out of the bottom three. Unlike their out-of-sorts hosts, Inter enjoyed another successful weekend. Serie A’s ‘comeback specialists’ lived up to their reputation on Sunday, with stoppage-time goals from Marcus Thuram and Piotr Zielinski propelling them to a come-from-behind 2-1 win over Fiorentina. There’s no room for complacency at San Siro, even though Cristian Chivu’s men sit at the table’s summit heading into this matchday. Sitting above Lazio on goal difference alone, the Nerazzurri can ill-afford a slip-up at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo if they’re to stay there before next weekend’s Milan derby. Match Preview Venezia Nicola’s winning start quickly faded away as Venezia slumped to their eight defeat in nine competitive matches this term (W1), failing to get on the scoresheet for the second time in their last four. In addition to their well-documented scoring woes, the Winged Lions have been notoriously prone to conceding in abundance, capitulating at least twice in seven of those eight losses. Against this backdrop, Venezia have been relatively solid at the back when playing on home turf, conceding one goal or fewer in 11 of their last 16 Serie A outings at the Pier Luigi Penzo. After beating Napoli in their most recent game here, they could win back-to-back top-flight home matches to nil for the first time since 1967. However, Venezia’s upcoming opponent cannot be more formidable. Since their last competitive win over Inter back in October 1999, Venezia have managed just one draw in eight meetings with the Nerazzurri (L7), losing the last five in a row by an aggregate score of 11-2. item.title: Runners swap streets for shopping malls as haze chokes Singapore
item.description: Fitness enthusiasts run inside a Singapore mall (Roslan RAHMAN) The pounding of running shoes echoes through a Singapore shopping mall as fitness enthusiasts desperate to exercise take refuge from choking haze. Smoke from wildfires in neighbouring Indonesia has sent air quality in the city-state plummeting to its worst levels in more than a decade in recent weeks, cancelling outdoor activities. Those seeking exercise, including runners training for international events, have found an unconventional alternative: air-conditioned shopping malls. On Saturday more than 80 runners turned the corridors of Marina Square shopping centre into makeshift running tracks, clocking laps past storefronts on two floors before shops opened for business. There are strict rules. "No sprinting, no overtaking, no shouting or yelling," Eugene Beh, 52, founder of Singapore Runners Club, told about 60 members before their run. Spitting and wiping sweat on the floor are also banned. Beh said they had to cancel several runs outdoors because of the haze, blown in by the wind from forest and peatland fires in Borneo and Sumatra. - 'Very mental' - Angeline Zeng, 57, who works in banking, completed 10 loops at the mall, or about 10 kilometres (six miles). With a half-marathon in Taipei in less than a week and a full marathon in December, Zeng needs to clock as much mileage as she can. Since treadmills at her neighbourhood gym are often full, she and her fellow runners were excited when they heard about the mall runs. "We were like, wow, we didn't expect that at all," she told AFP. "I love it because the aircon makes you feel like you're running overseas where there's cold temperatures, so it's really great," Zeng added. But she said that circling inside the mall becomes "boring" after a while. "Maybe for shorter runs this is okay but if you need to do long runs, maybe not so suitable," she said. Singapore Runners Club member Doris Tan, 42, said she thought running indoors would be a bit suffocating. "I didn't expect it to be so cool... but if you have to ask me, I still prefer outdoors," she told AFP. Paul Wong, a 54-year-old retiree from a club called X-Run, completed 21 loops inside the mall, or about 21 km. With just over a month until the Singapore International Marathon -– which many other fellow runners are also training for -– Wong would have to run up to 80 km per week, but the haze has forced him indoors. "For the last two weeks I've been running close to 100 kilometres on the treadmill. The longest I've run is 28 km for two and a half hours, it's very mental," Wong said. Eddie Chang, lead coach for X-Run, said they had to present a carefully laid-out plan to get approval from the mall for the runs. item.title: Jayson Tatum sends NBA warning after game-winning buzzer beater in Celtics win
item.description: Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images Jayson Tatum had a statement performance in the Boston Celtics’ win against the Brooklyn Nets, and he had a message for everyone after. All the talk recently surrounding Jayson Tatum has been about his relationship with his former co-star Jaylen Brown. The two have been going back and forth a bit after games, but the focus has been firmly away from what is happening on the floor. Tatum’s recent performance has brought the attention right back. In Tuesday night’s clash against the Brooklyn Nets, he had a whopping 40 points during the game. JT also iced the game in overtime with a buzzer beater that ended up winning the game for Boston. Jayson Tatum says he is ‘feeling like himself’ after Celtics win Tatum has been discussed quite a bit recently, and many fans and analysts have suggested that he might not be able to get back to his best after his injury. Since he returned towards the end of last season, JT hasn’t quite looked like his dominant self either, lending further credence to those takes. However, as they say in sports, class is permanent. And the 28-year-old has sent a message to the rest of the league, which they should take as a warning. “I’m starting to feel like my old self,” Tatum said after the game. Considering that his old self has been named to the All-NBA First Team four times, it should worry the Eastern Conference if JT is getting his confidence back. The Celtics star had 40 points, five rebounds, and eight assists against Brooklyn. This is a good start for him to get back to his best, but he will need to put together a string of these games if he wants the warning to really land. item.title: ‘Is anyone safe?’ – Jonathan Taylor’s wife shares fears about Colts future post Quenton Nelson trade
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor’s potential trade status has spooked his wife, Ayanna Taylor, after the team traded Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks. A year ago, the Colts were one of the best teams in the NFL, with Taylor looking like an MVP candidate by leading them to an 8-2 season record. Since then, the franchise has gone 2-12 and is 2-5 in the 2026 NFL season. With the team’s playoff hopes all but dead already, the Colts are expected to reshuffle their organisation, already firing team GM Chris Ballard, and now making player trades, making Taylor’s family uncomfortable about what may come next. Jonathan Taylor’s wife thinks Colts might trade them before next week Ayanna Taylor posted a story on Instagram where she is speaking into the camera and sharing her concerns about their future with the Colts after trading away a player like Nelson. “Is literally anyone safe on this team? It feels like rookie year all over again. My mind is spiralling. What does this mean for my husband and I? Do I need to start packing our bags? Are we going to be spending our daughter’s first Halloween together? Will we make it to gameday or was last week the last time my husband is putting on a Colts jersey? What are we going to do without Quenton Nelson?” Nelson was one of the key pieces of the Colts’ defence, and losing him is a visual representation of Indianapolis waving the white flag for this season. Taylor is inarguably their highest-value player. If the Colts are looking for a full organisational reset, moving on from the 27-year-old Taylor for a big haul of draft assets or young players could be their best move to officially embrace the rebuild. Taylor is having a fantastic season, registering 587 yards for eight touchdowns on 140 carries and 178 yards on 17 receptions for a total of 765 yards. Taylor has had multiple 90+-yard rushing games this season, trying to single-handedly spark the Colts’ offence amid struggles from QB Daniel Jones. With Nelson gone and the Colts looking to trade productive players away for future assets, the writing is on the wall for Taylor. However, his age also makes it realistic for the Colts to try and rebuild around him, so a trade away this season does not seem to be set in stone. Linebacker Bird Lloyd and the defense rose to the challenge, holding Sam Houston to zero touchdowns and zero second-half points. Many questions lingered after last week’s disappointing road loss to Delaware. Where Missouri State struggled against the Blue Hens, the Bears quickly cleaned up versus the Bearkats. The Bears allowed just 284 yards of offense, the lowest mark against an FBS opponent this season. After giving up 232 rushing yards to Delaware, Missouri State’s rush defense shined against Sam Houston. The Bearkats rushed for 26 yards, a season low for Missouri State. item.description: https://editorinleaf.com/maple-leafs-may-never-have-a-better-chance-to-trade-for-alexander-nikishin Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs, despite a clear need for blueline help, won’t be using Morgan Rielly as a trade chip, at least for now. Talk of trading Rielly is nothing new. And while rumors calmed down once this season began, the bottom line is that conventional wisdom suggests the Leafs would rather trade the veteran defenseman. Plus, one would think that his pretty decent start to this season would help make him more attractive on the trade market. Teams looking for a solid, veteran blueliner who could eat up some minutes might look into a trade. But it doesn’t seem that way. A predictive analysis model utilized by Heavy revealed that while a trade for a defenseman could have about a 25% chance of happening in the next seven days or so, such a deal won’t involve Morgan Rielly. The rationale for that assessment is simple: Rielly’s recent play, coupled with Chris Tanev’s absence, has actually made the 32-year-old a more valuable piece for the Maple Leafs so far this season. So, does that mean that Rielly can’t be traded? No, but it does reduce the likelihood of it happening significantly. Ultimately, GM John Chayka will be looking to prioritize internal solutions before seriously wading into the trade market. Morgan Rielly Has Had a Resurgent Start to the Season Another interesting situation complicating a potential Morgan Rielly trade is his resurgent season. He’s looked much better under Jim Hiller and has progressively regained some of the form he once showed. That unleashing of sorts has allowed Rielly to notch 10 assists in 14 games. If that doesn’t seem like much, well, Rielly is on par with Devon Toews, Lane Hutson, and Matthew Schaefer, and one point behind Cale Makar. That’s not bad when looking at the grander scheme of things . And while the Maple Leafs blueliner has yet to score a goal this season, one has to think that racking up 10 assists so far looks good. There’s also something else to consider: Rielly is averaging just under 20 minutes a night. He’s logging over 17 5v5, and a minute both on the power play and penalty kill. That could well be the difference here. Rielly isn’t getting nearly as much time on penalty kill duty, while allowing him to find more time playing against opponents at even strength. In a way, taking some of the burden off Morgan Rielly’s shoulders has helped him and the Maple Leafs. Could Maple Leafs Trade Rielly Anyway? That’s a fair question to ask. item.title: Alexander Volkanovski Explains Urgency to Finish Movsar Evloev
item.description: Alexander Volkanovski Movsar Evloev Getty UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski explained why he had so much urgency to finish Movsar Evloev at UFC 333. Volkanovski finished Evloev via second-round TKO in the co-main event of UFC 333 to defend his title for the second time during his second reign as the UFC featherweight champion. It was Volkanovski’s first finish since UFC 290 in July 2023, when he stopped Yair Rodriguez via TKO. Typically, the Aussie is content to outclass his opponents for five rounds and win a decision, but at UFC 333 against Evloev, it seemed clear that a finish was important to him. There is a reason for that. Alexander Volkanovski Explains Why UFC 333 Finish Was So Important Speaking to Brendan Bradford after arriving home in his native Australia, Volkanovski said that getting the finish over Evloev and making sure the fight finished in the second round was so important because he entered the fight with an illness , and he wasn’t confident that he would have his typically strong gas tank had the fight gone the distance. “I’m glad it was only two rounds cuz I was breathing a little heavier than usual. I had to take some big breaths… You could see that I started putting that pressure on, especially in the second round. It was like, alright, let’s start finding this finish. Again, I don’t want to go five rounds. I don’t know if these lungs can hold up being crook (sick) and all. And not only that, I started to see everything and knowing that the finish probably would come,” Volkanovski said (via Bloody Elbow ). Alexander Volkanovski’s Next UFC Challenge After Movsar Evloev Conquered Now that Volkanovski has taken care of the formerly undefeated Evloev, he will take some time off to rest and recover before jumping back into the Octagon in 2027 for his next fight. That could come either in the UFC featherweight division with a title defense against Jean Silva, Aljamain Sterling, or Kevin Vallejos, or Volkanovski may move up to 155 lbs and challenge UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje in what would be a true superfight between two of the sport’s biggest fan favorites.
